So my old ISP was bought out about 5 years ago by another ISP. In the last couple of months the new ISP has been charging me late fees because they have a different payment schedule than the last ISP but didn't feel like telling me for 4 years. Now the new ISP doesn't have contracts and says that the contract I had with the previous company doesn't mean shit. Yet 4 months ago when I called in about not getting enough speed according to my contract (that's apparently not valid) within 24 hours I got a boost in speed. A month later now and my speed boost is gone and when I call in about it they claim they have no record of it and plead with me to let it go. On top of that now I got told at least 4 time "You do not have a contract with us!" So does that mean if I don't have a contract that they can't charge late fees? Anybody have any loopholes out of a "contractless" situation? By saying it's contractless they have the ability to set the terms as they see fit, but does it give me any negotiating power?
"You don't have a contract, we don't give out contracts!" Help with an ISP pl0x

Matter is easily resolved if you retained your paperwork.

I had this problem years ago when my local telecom got bought out but I had all the documentation to prove that I was a customer under a specific plan.

I have the old contract with a signature and everything, including my differing payment period and speed/price. They just straight up told me it doesn't mean shit because it's expired and they don't have contracts so it won't be honored.

"It doesn't mean shit" cuts both ways. Tell them that's wonderful news, and since there's no contract there's nothing defined for late payments or even a payment schedule. They can make up fees all they want, it doesn't mean shit.

Demand something new in writing from them before they see another penny.

Edit - any time you call them up, record the conversation. Tell them you are doing so "for your records" with a smile.

Are you in the US? Do not call them anymore. Send them a certified letter detailing your complaint, and keep record of when it's delivered. Only communicate with them in writing. In the US you have the right to demand communication in writing from a company you are doing business with.

Let them know in the letter that you would like them to continue honoring your valid contract. Make sure you state that you never received notice of cancellation or renegotiation of contract terms and you would like to be mailed copies of what plan they currently have you signed up for. Also state that you have been charged late fee in error and you expect to be refunded. Also state you would like to resolve this issue without a third party.

If they continue to call be very firm that you want only communication in writing from them.

They are legally obligated to honor contracts of a company they purchased. A lot of companies try to bully people with lifetime contracts.

I called them again, I'm sorry, but they waived the lastest late fee and are sending out a tech to my house to evaluate the equipment. But if I'm still unsatisfied I'm to call the office manager personally to complain. I guess it's a step in the right direction.
